docs.title: Theatre Notes
docs.text: General professional theatre practice: the things that are true regardless of which building you are standing in.

docs.title: What belongs here, and what does not
docs.text:
This is the deliberate counterpart to a venue site. A venue site documents ONE operation: its rooms, its power, its house rules. This one documents the CRAFT, so a venue page can point at a general practice instead of restating it and then slowly disagreeing with the last place that restated it.

The boundary is worth defending, because it is the one that will blur:

  • Here: how a thing is generally done, why a convention exists, vocabulary.
  • Not here: any figure, rule or contact that belongs to one building.

If a page cannot be written without naming a specific venue, it is a venue page.

docs.title: Writing for this site
docs.text:
The authoring contract is shared across every site in this family and is documented once, on the template site, as a live example of every rule it states:

  • The frontmatter contract
  • Writing a page: callouts, tabs, tables

docs.title: Paper tech
docs.text:
Walking every cue in the prompt book with the design team before anybody is standing on stage waiting.

Owner Stage manager Frequency Once per production, before the first tech rehearsal Trigger Cues exist on paper and have not yet been run in the room Systems Prompt book, cue sheets, design paperwork

This page exists as the first real content on this site and as a demonstration: it is a procedure, it names an owner, and the table above is drawn from its frontmatter by the type rather than typed by hand.

The cost of skipping it

Every cue not agreed on paper gets agreed in the room instead, with the full company on the clock. It is the cheapest hour in the process and the easiest one to cut.

docs.title: Why it is general and not venue-specific
docs.text:
Nothing above names a building. That is the test for whether a page belongs on this site: a venue's page can link here for the practice and add only what is true of its own room.
